does: Dissolves the browned layer stuck to a hot pan with a splash of liquid, turning it into the base of a sauce.

intro.what: Deglazing loosens the browned layer on a pan with liquid and a spoon.
intro.why: It shows how the brown traces left by cooking can become the base of a sauce.

how: Pour off the fat, and keep everything brown that sticks to the pan.
Soften a little shallot or garlic in the pan first, if the sauce calls for it.
Take the pan off the flame to add wine or spirits, then put it back.
Scrape the bottom with a wooden spoon as the liquid boils, until the pan is clean and the liquid has turned brown.

cues.text: A sharp hiss and a burst of steam when the liquid hits the pan.
The bottom of the pan comes clean under the spoon and the liquid darkens.
The raw smell of the wine goes as it boils.

mistakes.mistake: Deglazing a pan whose fond has burnt black, which makes a bitter sauce.
mistakes.fix: Taste a scrap of the fond first. If it is bitter, wipe the pan out and build the sauce without it.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving all the fat in, so that the sauce is greasy and will not come together.
mistakes.fix: Pour the fat off first. The flavour is in the brown bits, not in the fat.

quiz.question: What does deglazing turn into a sauce base?
choices: The brown layer stuck to the pan.
Only the fat floating in the pan.
Blackened residue from any burnt pan.
quiz.because: Liquid dissolves the browned layer, or fond, and carries it into the sauce base.

quiz.question: What do you do with the excess fat before deglazing?
choices: Pour it off while keeping the browned bits.
Wipe out the browned bits and keep the fat.
quiz.because: Excess fat can leave the sauce greasy. Pour it off while keeping the browned layer for flavour.

quiz.question: Which change shows that the browned layer is loosening?
choices: The pan stays coated and the liquid stays unchanged.
Clear fat collects around an untouched layer.
The pan comes clean under the spoon and the liquid darkens.
quiz.because: As the browned layer dissolves, the pan comes clean under the spoon and the liquid takes on its colour.

quiz.question: The fond has burnt black and tastes bitter. What would you do?
choices: Add more liquid to preserve all of it.
Wipe it out and build the sauce without it.
Scrape harder to include the black layer.
quiz.because: Bitter, burnt fond would carry bitterness into the sauce. Wipe it out and build the sauce without it.

comes_after.why: There is nothing to deglaze until a sear has left a fond.
